response.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM Invoices AS i JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id GROUP BY c.gender), shares AS (SELECT gender, invoice_count, invoice_count * 1.0 / SUM(invoice_count) OVER () AS share FROM gender_counts), compared AS (SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;

assumptions.assumption: Invoices whose matched customer has a NULL gender form one group, so every matched invoice contributes to the total.

alternatives.interpretation: Treat NULL as an unknown value rather than a gender, and exclude those invoices from the counts and total.
alternatives.sql: WITH gender_counts AS (SELECT c.gender, COUNT(*) AS invoice_count FROM Invoices AS i JOIN Orders AS o ON o.order_id = i.order_id JOIN Customers AS c ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.gender IS NOT NULL GROUP BY c.gender), shares AS (SELECT gender, invoice_count, invoice_count * 1.0 / SUM(invoice_count) OVER () AS share FROM gender_counts), compared AS (SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT gender, invoice_count, share, share - average_share AS share_above_average FROM compared WHERE share > average_share;
